findings.title: Unsubscribe action crashes when no TopicUser row exists
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil if the user has never visited or tracked the topic, so `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError and the request returns a 500. This happens whenever a user gets a notification email without a topic_users row, for example a mailing-list-mode user. It should use `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row if missing.

findings.title: State-changing action on a GET request
findings.body: Visiting the GET route `t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe` immediately changes the notification level. Email link scanners, prefetchers and crawlers can therefore unsubscribe or mute users without their consent. The action also toggles: a second visit, such as a page refresh, moves the user from regular to muted. The action is not idempotent.

findings.title: Anonymous users get an error and no redirect to login
findings.body: The `unsubscribe` action requires a logged-in user via `ensure_logged_in`. A user who clicks the email link while logged out gets an error and is not sent back after login. Also, `current_user.id` is used with no guard.

findings.title: Redirect for slug-less URLs doesn't preserve format
findings.body: The redirect to `unsubscribe_url` is built from `url`, which is the absolute URL without the format. The `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe` route therefore redirects to the slugged URL, and the first visit's state change is skipped in that redirect branch. This is inconsistent.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url missing for other callers of unsubscribe_link
findings.body: The `unsubscribe_link` translation now requires `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Other emails that set `add_unsubscribe_link` without `unsubscribe_url`, such as digest or other mailers, will raise an I18n missing-interpolation error or print a literal placeholder. Only `send_notification_email` was updated to pass it.

findings.title: Typo in property name and unescaped HTML in title
findings.body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText`, which is a typo, and the same name is used in the template. The template renders it with triple-stash (`{{{ }}}`), and `fancyTitle` is HTML-escaped server-side, so this is acceptable. It still relies on that escaping.
